Command: Rest on the first day of Tabernacles
Summary: The first day of the Feast of Tabernacles is a holy convocation of rest, opening seven days of dwelling in booths.
Commandment: Keep the first day of Tabernacles as a holy convocation and rest on it.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The rest opened the harvest feast that remembered Israel's booths in the wilderness. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
